events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding during morning high tides expected. For the High Surf
Advisory, dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves of 5
to 7 feet, except peaking at 6 to 9 feet on Monday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Flooded sandy beach areas and moderate beach
erosion possible. Localized and shallow flooding of beach
parking lots, bike paths, and walkways. Isolated damage is
unlikely, but cannot be discounted.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.0 to 7.3 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning. Surf and coastal flooding impacts peak on
Monday. Additonal products will likely be needed through the
week.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 10 to 16 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of near 7.0 ft (MLLW) are
expected each morning. The High Surf and Coastal Flood
Advisories may need to be extended through the week.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding during
morning high tides, as well as dangerous rip currents and
breaking waves due to elevated surf up to 4 to 6 feet
expected, especially across west facing beaches.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Malibu Coast and
Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.2 to 7.4 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning. Surf and coastal flooding impacts peak on
Monday. Since the large swell is from the west, south facing
areas such as Malibu and Long Beach will be less affected unlike
the previous events where the swell was from the south.

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Iowa...

Iowa River at Marengo affecting Benton and Iowa Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Iowa River at Marengo.

* WHEN...Until late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, water reaches the bottom of the levee
surrounding Marengo. Water affects low lying agricultural land
along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 AM CST Monday the stage was 15.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage this
evening and continue falling to 10.5 feet Monday, November 16.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Kimble, TX; Mason, TX; Menard, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Kimble County in west central Texas...
Western Mason County in west central Texas...
Southeastern Menard County in west central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM CST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Some low-water crossings may become
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 901 AM CST, the public reported heavy rain in low water
crossings. This will cause small stream flooding. Between 2.5 and
3.5 inches of rain have fallen over the past 2-3 days.
- Low water crossings are the most likely place to experience minor
flooding. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
South Llano River State Park, US-377 near Telegraph, Ranch Road
2291 north of I-10, Ranch Road 385 from US-377 to US-290, Farm to
Market 2169 near Junction, The Intersection Of Us-83 And Ranch
Road 1773, and Us-83 Near The Kerr-Kimble County Line
- This includes Interstate 10 between Mile Markers 435 and 477.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
